text: Residence hall on the north side of campus near the sports fields.

name: Eliot Hall
text: Reed's original 1912 academic building: humanities and social science classrooms and faculty offices, the admission office and the chapel.

name: Old Dorm Block
text: Reed's original 1912 Tudor Gothic dormitory, divided into eight halls (Abington, Doyle, Eastport, Kerr, Ladd, Quincy, Westport, Winch).

name: Student Union
text: Large hall for dances, concerts, student events and Renn Fayre; houses Paradox Café, a coffee shop.

name: Student Center
text: Student activities office and multicultural resource center: club support, event planning and identity-based community programs.

name: Gray Campus Center
text: Commons dining hall, bookstore, mail services and SEEDS (community service and engagement office).

name: Kaul Auditorium
text: Main auditorium for concerts, lectures, convocation and large events; includes Gray Lounge for receptions.

name: Physical Plant
text: Facilities Services: maintenance, grounds, custodial and trades shops that keep the campus running.

name: Eric V. Hauser Memorial Library
text: Eric V. Hauser Memorial Library: stacks, study spaces, special collections and archives, thesis tower; also the Cooley Art Gallery for exhibitions.

name: Vollum College Center
text: Lecture hall (used for large lectures such as the Humanities 110 lectures), faculty offices and a lounge.

name: Greywood Hall
text: Alumni and parent relations, campus information and career services (Center for Life Beyond Reed).

name: Educational Technology Center
text: Instructional technology support, computer labs and media services for classes and faculty.

text: Coed residence hall named for a former Reed president.

name: Foster Hall
text: Coed residence hall with divided doubles; the other half of the original Foster-Scholz.

name: Anna Mann Hall
text: Historic 1920 residence hall by A.E. Doyle, originally for women and now coed (about 32 residents).

name: Scholz Hall
text: Coed residence hall built 1954–55; originally half of the Foster-Scholz men's dorm.

text: Newest Cross Canyon residence hall (1998), named for a former Reed president; mostly first-years.

text: Grove residence hall (2008) with house-style living.

name: Sequoia House
text: One of the four Grove residence halls (completed 2008), with house-like suites and shared kitchens and common rooms.

name: Aspen House
text: Grove residence hall (2008); also contains a multipurpose classroom and Caffè Paradiso, a café.

name: Bidwell House
text: Grove residence hall (2008) with house-style living.

name: Biology
text: L.E. Griffin Memorial Biology Building: biology labs, classrooms and an auditorium.

name: Chemistry
text: A.A. Knowlton chemistry building: teaching and research labs, classrooms and faculty offices.

name: Greenwood Hall
text: Greenwood Hall.

name: Performing Arts Building
text: Opened 2013: theatre, dance and music departments with a studio theatre, black box, rehearsal halls, scene and costume shops. Since 2010: Built after this 2010 map; replaces functions of #13 and #17.

name: Reed College Sports Center
text: Gym, indoor pool, fitness rooms and courts; physical education classes, club sports and intramurals.

name: Physics
text: Physics department classrooms, teaching labs and research labs.

name: Studio Arts
text: Studio art department: painting, sculpture, printmaking and photo studios, critiques; Feldenheimer Gallery shows student and visiting work.

name: Prexy Hall
text: Music building on this map (a former president's residence): practice rooms, lessons and music offices. Since 2010: Music largely moved to the Performing Arts Building in 2013.

name: Parker House
text: 1929 Arts and Crafts house bought by Reed in 2005; three guest rooms for visiting lecturers, academics and trustees, plus meeting rooms for retreats, faculty dinners and Gray Fund student dinners.

name: Dorothy Johansen House
text: Former home of alumna, history professor and archivist Dorothy Johansen; now houses academic support services (tutoring, writing and study help).

name: Garden House
text: Small themed house (about ten students) focused on sustainability and environmental justice; residents tend gardens and run related programming.

name: Canyon House
text: Residence hall that serves as an extension of the Garden House sustainability and environmental justice community.

name: German House
text: German language house (8 singles) with a language scholar; hosts campuswide cultural events.

name: French House
text: French language house with a language scholar; hosts films, meals and concerts.

name: Russian House
text: Small residence where students practice Russian, with a live-in native-speaker language scholar; hosts films, meals and cultural events.

name: Spanish House
text: Spanish language house with a language scholar; its plaza is a shared gathering space for the language houses.

name: Chinese House
text: Chinese language house with a language scholar; tea, cooking and cultural activities. Since 2010: Reed has since moved the Chinese House to sit closer to the other language houses; language scholars now also include Arabic.

name: Farm House
text: Small house-style residence hall.

name: Reed Warehouse
text: Storage for theatre sets, props and costumes plus general college warehousing and receiving. Since 2010: Most theatre production work moved to the Performing Arts Building in 2013.

name: Trillium
text: Reed's largest residence hall, opened 2019 near the Grove where tennis courts used to be; about 180 first-year students, LEED Platinum. Since 2010: Built after this 2010 map.
